options.description: Keep one repo. Cut release/0.33.x for fixes only. On master, each operation gets its observable spec, model and conformance cells before any backend beyond Memory moves onto the kernel. Tooling, backlog and history stay together.

options.description: Freeze this repo at v0.33.0 and do mostly spec work in a fork. Clean break and no old-spec baggage, but backlog, CI and tooling are duplicated and specs go long stretches without code to check them.

options.label: In-repo, no gate
options.description: Carry on as now with RFC-0017's D3 steps and new specs alongside. Least disruption, but nothing stops implementation from running ahead of the specs.

questions.question: May the new observable-semantics specs change the public Store API's behaviour relative to 0.33?

options.label: Yes, toward v1 (Recommended)
options.description: Specs define the target semantics. Where 0.33 behaves differently, that's a recorded breaking change for v1. Gives the spec work real freedom, and every break needs a migration note.

options.label: Signatures fixed only
options.description: Method names and signatures stay as in 0.33, but observable behaviour (errors, stream lifetime, consistency) may change. A middle path: user code still compiles but may behave differently.

options.label: Describe 0.33 as is
options.description: Specs formalize today's behaviour and record mismatches as bugs. Safest for users, but it bakes in design decisions you want to revisit.

questions.question: During the spec-first phase, which evidence is allowed?

options.label: Models, spikes, probes (Recommended)
options.description: Formal models (Alloy, Lean, Dafny, TLA+), executable reference models with property tests, and live backend probes, as in PR 1173. No production kernel or driver code.

options.label: Formal models only
options.description: Proofs and model checking only, no executable spikes or backend probes. Purest, but nothing grounds the specs in real backend behaviour.

options.label: Plus Memory reference
options.description: Also keep the Memory driver on the kernel as a living reference that each spec is checked against. Closest to an oracle, but production code keeps moving.

questions.question: What happens to specs 001 to 050 during the reset?

options.label: Superseded per section (Recommended)
options.description: They stay in force as the description of current behaviour. Each new spec names which old sections it supersedes, and those are retired when the new one is accepted. No gap in coverage.

options.label: Frozen as legacy
options.description: All marked legacy and describing 0.33 only, with no further edits. New specs start from a clean slate in a separate series. Clean, but two spec sets coexist.

options.label: Inventory, then rewrite
options.description: Treated as an inventory of decisions to harvest, then removed once the new specs cover them. Most radical; history stays in git only.

questions.question: Where should the spec-first work live?

options.label: Master + 0.33.x branch (Recommended)
options.description: Freeze on release/0.33.x for fixes only; the spec work runs on master. One backlog, one CI, one tooling stack.

options.label: Fork
options.description: This repo stays at v0.33.0 and the spec work moves to a fork. Clean break; the sdd/ tooling, backlog and CI have to be carried over and then kept in sync or abandoned.

options.label: Decide in the RFC
options.description: Leave it open now and let the RFC compare the options with their costs.

questions.question: In what order should the specs be built?

options.label: read() slice first (Recommended)
options.description: Spec read() end to end first: the parts of keys, errors and resource lifecycle it needs, its call contract, stream lifecycle and consistency. That proves the method on one operation before scaling; the shared layers grow from real need.

options.label: Foundations first
options.description: Finish the shared layers first (key model from PR 1173, error model, resource and session lifecycle, consistency model), then all operations on top. Cleaner layering, but the shared layers get designed without an operation pushing on them.

options.label: All operations at once
options.description: A call contract for every public method in one pass, then lifecycles and consistency. Fast coverage, but the most likely to repeat 003's contradictions.

questions.question: When may kernel and driver implementation resume?

options.label: Core set specced (Recommended)
options.description: Once read, write, list, delete and metadata plus the shared layers are accepted. Covers what every backend needs, while the remaining operations (copy, move, glob, atomic) follow under the same gate.

options.label: Per operation
options.description: Each operation's implementation resumes as soon as its own spec is accepted. Fastest feedback, but implementation pressure creeps back into the later specs.

options.label: Whole surface
options.description: No implementation until every public operation is specced. Purest, but the longest stretch without real code to check against.

questions.question: Where do the observable decisions (the R-1 to R-6 kind) get recorded?

options.label: Research doc per spec (Recommended)
options.description: As with spec 051 and PR 1173 § 6: the spec holds only the clauses, and a companion research doc holds each decision with the rejected options and why. The interview logs under sdd/decisions/ back them.

options.label: One ADR per decision
options.description: Every observable choice becomes an ADR. Maximum visibility, but likely dozens of small ADRs per operation.

options.label: Inside the spec
options.description: A Rationale note on each clause. Everything in one place, but it mixes the why into the what, which SPEC-DESIGN.md keeps apart.

questions.question: Which backends must the backend-qualified guarantees cover in the first pass?

options.label: Representative set (Recommended)
options.description: Memory as the reference, plus one of each kind: hierarchical (Local), flat object store (S3), session-based (SFTP). Every qualification axis gets exercised; the remaining backends map onto those profiles later.

options.label: All built-in backends
options.description: Every backend's profile stated from the start. Complete, but most of the effort goes into probing rather than semantics.

options.label: Abstract only
options.description: Specs define the axes (stable or not, lifetime, and so on) without naming any backend's profile yet. Lightest, but nothing checks that the axes fit real backends.

questions.question: Old specs 001-050: adopt supersede-per-section with deletion once a file is empty, plus a '0.33 behaviour, being superseded' header?

options.label: Yes, as proposed (Recommended)
options.description: Section-level retirement, file deleted when empty, register entry maps old IDs to new. No coverage gap and no lasting legacy set.

options.label: Supersede, keep files
options.description: Same, but emptied files stay as stubs that point to their successors. Old links never break, at the cost of clutter.

options.label: Supersede, no header
options.description: Retire per section without marking the old specs. Less churn now, but readers can't tell 0.33 behaviour from the v1 target.

questions.question: How should the link from abstract axes to real backends be recorded (decision 6)?

options.label: Profile table + probes (Recommended)
options.description: One profile table per axis, one row per representative backend (Memory, Local, S3, SFTP), each cell citing a dated probe or vendor-doc source. The format of PR 1173's backend-path-authorities doc. Lives beside the spec, not in it.

options.label: Conformance cells
options.description: Each backend's profile is a set of declared cells in the conformance suite, checked by running it. Executable, but it needs a harness during a phase that has no production drivers.

options.label: Per-backend spec section
options.description: Each backend spec (008, 009, ...) states its value on every axis. Familiar, but it puts reality back into the specs being rewritten.

questions.question: How do the v1 breaking changes reach users?

options.label: Single 1.0.0 cut (Recommended)
options.description: master carries no release until the v1 surface is implemented. 0.33.x gets fixes only. One migration guide, built up from the breaking-change records.

options.label: 0.x pre-releases
options.description: Ship 0.34, 0.35 and so on as operations land, each with its own breaks. Earlier feedback, but users migrate repeatedly.

options.label: Decide later
options.description: Leave it to the RFC's open questions; the spec work doesn't depend on it yet.

questions.question: What is today's conformance suite during the reset?

options.label: Evidence of 0.33 (Recommended)
options.description: It documents what 0.33 does. Each new spec checks its clauses against it: agreement is evidence, disagreement becomes a recorded breaking change or a bug. Nothing is deleted until the new suite replaces those cells.

options.label: v1 oracle from start
options.description: Its cells are rewritten to the v1 target as specs land, even though nothing implements v1 yet. Red until implementation resumes.

options.label: Frozen with 0.33.x
options.description: It lives on the release branch only; master starts a new suite with the new specs. Clean, but it loses the old-vs-new comparison.

questions.question: Old specs 001-050: adopt supersede-per-section with deletion once a file is empty, plus a '0.33 behaviour, being superseded' header?

options.label: Yes, as proposed (Recommended)
options.description: Section-level retirement, file deleted when empty, register entry maps old IDs to new. No coverage gap and no lasting legacy set.

options.label: Supersede, keep files
options.description: Same, but emptied files stay as stubs that point to their successors. Old links never break, at the cost of clutter.

options.label: Supersede, no header
options.description: Retire per section without marking the old specs. Less churn now, but readers can't tell 0.33 behaviour from the v1 target.

Where does the skill stop?

options.label: Decisions + research doc (Recommended)
options.description: It ends with every axis decided or explicitly open, written to the operation's research doc. Spec drafting is a separate step, so this skill stays small and reusable.

options.label: Through spec draft
options.description: It also drafts the spec clauses from the decisions. One flow end to end, but it mixes deciding and writing, and the skill grows large.

options.label: Decisions only, in chat
options.description: Interview only; the logs are the record and you write the doc. Lightest, but the decisions sit in a JSONL file rather than in a readable doc.

questions.question: Where do the questions come from?

options.label: Fixed axes + grounding (Recommended)
options.description: A fixed list of observation axes in the skill, filtered by what the repo already decides. Reproducible across operations, and nothing gets missed silently.

options.label: Free per operation
options.description: The model derives the questions per operation, as in the chat. Flexible, but coverage depends on the run.

options.label: Axes as a reviewed doc
options.description: The axis list is its own authority doc under sdd/, and the skill references it. Single source of truth, but one more doc to maintain.

questions.question: How strictly should questions be one at a time?

options.label: Dependent: one at a time (Recommended)
options.description: Questions that build on an earlier answer come one per round; independent axes are batched up to 4. Keeps the chat's depth without serial round trips where they don't help.

options.label: Always one at a time
options.description: Exactly like the chat. Maximum focus per decision, but many rounds.

options.label: Batch per axis group
options.description: Up to 4 questions per round, grouped by axis. Fast, but later answers can't build on earlier ones.

questions.question: Working name?

options.label: /observe (Recommended)
options.description: Names the core: what an observer can see. Short.

options.label: /semantics
options.description: Names the outcome: an operation's semantics.

options.label: /decide-op
options.description: Names the mechanism: a decision round for one operation.

questions.question: How should the unprimed context be enforced?

options.label: Fresh agent + path hook (Recommended)
options.description: The skill runs in a fresh agent, and a PreToolUse hook denies reads outside an allowlist. Enforced and testable; it costs a hook script and its tests.

options.label: Fresh session, no hook
options.description: A fresh session with a strict prompt only. Simple, but you'd be fighting drift again, as with spec 051.

options.label: No repo tools at all
options.description: The design agent gets no file tools; the skill passes the allowed inputs in the prompt. Strongest isolation, but large inputs bloat the prompt and nothing can be looked up mid-session.

questions.question: Who curates the allowlist?

options.label: Fixed core + your additions (Recommended)
options.description: A fixed core (spec 051, accepted abstract research, the operation's decision doc), plus files you name at the start of each session. Reproducible, and you keep control.

options.label: You, per session
options.description: No default; you name every input each time. Maximum control, more friction.

options.label: Fixed only
options.description: Only the fixed core, no additions. Most reproducible, but it can't take in a new accepted doc without changing the skill.

questions.question: Where does the skill stop?
At which point does a flow's output join the ground?

options.label: After the spec is accepted (Recommended)
options.description: The spec and its formal model are accepted; the 0.33 comparison isn't needed for admission because it never changes decisions. Next operations can build on it early.

options.label: After decisions recorded
options.description: As soon as the research doc's decisions are final, before spec drafting. Fastest, but unformalized decisions could contradict each other later.

options.label: After the full flow
options.description: Only after the comparison too. Most conservative, but the comparison would block progress even though it can't change anything.

questions.question: How is a ground artifact reopened when a later flow finds it wrong?

options.label: Explicit reopen decision (Recommended)
options.description: The current session stops on that point, records a reopen decision, and the artifact goes through its own flow again. Flows that depend on it are flagged in the register.

options.label: Fix in current flow
options.description: The current session revises the ground artifact directly and records it. Faster, but a flow about write ends up quietly changing read.

options.label: Never reopen
options.description: Ground is append-only; a conflict is resolved by adding a refining artifact. Simplest history, but errors accumulate as layers of exceptions.

Should the format research run unprimed too?

options.label: Unprimed + lessons brief (Recommended)
options.description: A fresh agent researches prior art without the repo's specs. You or I add a short brief listing the repo's documented failure modes (prose growth, backend-spec bloat, backlog item growth) as requirements, not as designs to copy.

options.label: Fully unprimed
options.description: No repo input at all; only your problem statement. Most independent, but it may optimize for problems you don't have.

options.label: With repo authority docs
options.description: It may read SPEC-DESIGN.md, the research docs on spec design and level of detail, and spec 051. Better fit with what exists, but risks anchoring on today's approach.

questions.question: How do we compare the candidate formats?

options.label: Bake-off on read() (Recommended)
options.description: 2-3 shortlisted forms each encode the same read() contract, scored on fixed criteria (checkability, readability, authoring cost, drift resistance). This needs the read() decisions first, so the read() /observe session comes before the bake-off.

options.label: Paper comparison
options.description: A prior-art survey and criteria matrix only. Faster, but formats look better on paper than when used.

options.label: Bake-off on spec 051
options.description: Re-encode the accepted spec 051 in the candidate forms. Available now, but it's pure structure and doesn't test single calls or lifetimes.

questions.question: Where does the format decision live?

options.label: Own RFC after research (Recommended)
options.description: Research doc → its own RFC that amends SPEC-DESIGN.md. The reset RFC references it as a dependency. Keeps each RFC focused.

options.label: Inside the reset RFC
options.description: One RFC covers process and format. A single decision point, but a large RFC that blocks on the research.

options.label: Amend SPEC-DESIGN.md directly
options.description: Research feeds directly into an amendment of the authority doc via ADR. Less ceremony, but the format change gets no RFC-level discussion.
